Package size from the chains' price-file fields, for products whose name carries no size (half the chains truncate names to ~20 characters) - sizeFromChainFields + resolveChainFieldSize (src/catalog/size.js), called from scripts/build-products.mjs's pickSize-area fallback only when (a) no chain NAME yields a size and (b) the product's FINAL isWeighted (majority across chains) is false - a weighed product never gets a size from these fields even when one chain's own row is not itself weighted (owner's hard rule, 10.10.2026: isWeighted is the single source of truth for the price unit). Built from data/local/size-unit-table.json and data/local/size-from-chain-fields-report.md (10.10.2026, measured per chain against data/prices/<chain>/PriceFull.xml, validated against parseSize(name) ground truth - NOT the UnitOfMeasurePrice field, which this analysis found does not need to be checked: ramilevy's Quantity validates fine against real package weights even though its UnitOfMeasurePrice is simply ItemPrice/100 on every row, unrelated to quantity).

Semantics: `quantityIs` 'amount' = Quantity already IS the package amount in the target `unit` (e.g. '100 גרם' -> Quantity=250 for a 250 g item) and reports the SINGLE sales unit on a multipack, not the pack total (carrefour's 18×200g box shows Quantity=200). 'amountInUnit' = Quantity is in the basis's own larger unit (קילוגרם/ליטר) and `scale` (1000) converts to g/ml - and on this basis Quantity already IS the full multipack total (a 6×330ml pack reports 1.98, i.e. 6×0.33). 'count' = Quantity is a pack-unit count ('יחידות'/'יחידה') - trustworthy on hazihinam, mck and shukcity only (every other chain writes Quantity=1 on real multipacks under this basis, so their tables below simply omit a יחידות-type bucket - the allow-list IS the set of chains whose table below has one, never widened by `fallback`). hazihinam leaves UnitOfMeasure blank on every row; its bucket keys are 'UQ:<UnitQty value>' and sizeFromChainFields only tries that fallback when the UnitOfMeasure lookup itself comes up empty. `victory` is excluded (excludedChains): its UnitOfMeasure text is corrupted on disk (literal '?' bytes baked into the stored file, not a decoding bug) and its UnitQty is a near-constant default, so it carries no usable signal.

Resolution across chains (resolveChainFieldSize, called with one candidate per chain FAMILY - siblings sharing a storefront are deduped exactly like familyVotes dedupes names, so carrefour/ybitan/quik or yochananof/yochananof_b never inflate a single feed's vote threefold): reliability-weighted majority on the total amount (value×count), grouping candidates within 5% of each other; the group with the highest summed `chainReliability` weight wins. If the runner-up group's weight is within 0.15 of the winner's AND they disagree by more than 5% on the total, the result is null (routed to review, docs/QUESTIONS-FOR-NAOR.md style warn line - one product never blocks the publish) rather than guessed. `chainReliability` is the n-weighted average match-rate across ALL of that chain's measured buckets (trusted and skipped) from the report - how good its fields are overall, used only as a cross-chain vote weight, not as a per-item accept/reject gate (that gate is simply whether a bucket exists in the chain's own table at all). Measured gain (10.10.2026, before the owner's isWeighted hard rule narrowed the population further): 7,594 of 18,883 non-weighed, GTIN-bearing, name-sizeless products get a size this way; chains disagree (by resolveChainFieldSize's definition) on only 16.7% of the cases where 2+ chains both have a candidate. `fallback` (the universal '*' bucket) applies only to a chain entirely absent from `chains` (e.g. a future 15th chain before its own measurement round) - it is never merged into an existing chain's table, so it can never restore a basis that chain deliberately omits (the יחידות allow-list above all). Additive config, not part of the published pipeline contract - see docs/PIPELINE-CONTRACT.md's `size` paragraph.
